title: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers

learn.hook: Whether it is snowy mountains, deep seas or the open sky, someone is keeping watch over India every minute.
points: 'A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers' honours the men and women who protect our country. Homage means deep respect shown to honour someone.
India's armed forces are the Army (land), the Navy (sea) and the Air Force (air).
The President of India is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces.
Army Day is on 15 January, Air Force Day on 8 October and Navy Day on 4 December.
Soldiers also help people during floods, earthquakes and other disasters with rescue and relief.

example.q: A flood hits a village. Which forces might help, and how?
steps: The Army can rescue people and set up relief camps.
The Navy can send boats and divers.
The Air Force can fly helicopters to drop food and lift people to safety.
example.answer: All three can help: the Army on land, the Navy with boats and divers, and the Air Force with helicopters.

learn.reallife: On Republic Day, the parade on Kartavya Path in New Delhi shows marching contingents of the Army, Navy and Air Force.

games.title: Armed forces facts
items: The Navy protects India's seas and coasts.
The Navy guards the sea.
The Prime Minister is the Supreme Commander of India's armed forces.
The President of India is the Supreme Commander.
Soldiers help people during floods and earthquakes.
They carry out rescue and relief work.
Army Day is celebrated on 15 January.
It is celebrated every year on 15 January.
The Air Force mainly guards the deep sea.
The Air Force guards the skies; the Navy guards the sea.

quiz.q: Which force guards India's seas?
quiz.explain: The Navy protects our seas and coastline.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the three forces

quiz.q: Who is the Supreme Commander of India's armed forces?
quiz.explain: The Constitution makes the President the Supreme Commander of the armed forces.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the head of government commands the forces

quiz.q: On which date is Army Day celebrated?
quiz.explain: Army Day is on 15 January. The other dates are Republic Day, Independence Day and Gandhi Jayanti.
quiz.mistake: Confuses Army Day with other national days

quiz.q: On which date is Air Force Day celebrated?
quiz.explain: Air Force Day is on 8 October.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the days of the three forces

quiz.q: On which date is Navy Day celebrated?
quiz.explain: Navy Day is celebrated on 4 December.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the days of the forces

quiz.q: What does 'homage' mean?
options: deep respect shown to honour someone
quiz.explain: To pay homage is to honour someone with respect.
quiz.mistake: Guesses from the sound 'home'

quiz.q: Apart from guarding the borders, soldiers also:
options: help people during floods and earthquakes
quiz.explain: The armed forces carry out rescue and relief work during disasters.
quiz.mistake: Does not know about disaster relief

quiz.q: Which force flies fighter jets to defend India's skies?
quiz.explain: Defending the skies is the main job of the Air Force.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the forces

teach.ask: Gappu saw soldiers marching on Republic Day. Who are our armed forces, and what do they do?
teach.praise: Salute! The Army, Navy and Air Force keep us safe on land, sea and sky!
teach.nudge: Name the three forces, and tell me what they protect.

learn.hook: 'Param Vir' means 'the bravest of the brave' — the name of India's highest wartime gallantry award.
points: Patriotism means love for one's country; a patriot is a person who loves and serves the country.
Sacrifice means giving up something precious for the sake of others.
Gallantry and valour both mean great bravery. Valiant means very brave; its opposite is cowardly.
The Param Vir Chakra is India's highest wartime gallantry award; the Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime gallantry award.
The National War Memorial in New Delhi honours soldiers who gave their lives for the nation.

example.q: Why do people stand in silence at a war memorial?
steps: A memorial reminds us of soldiers who gave their lives.
Silence is a way of showing deep respect.
It helps us remember their sacrifice.
example.answer: To show respect and remember the soldiers' sacrifice for the nation.

learn.reallife: Many schools collect money on Armed Forces Flag Day (7 December) for the welfare of soldiers and their families.

games.title: Words of honour
pairs: giving up something precious for others
a person who loves and serves the country
something built to remember people or events

items.text: The soldier was awarded a medal for his ___.
A ___ loves and serves the country.
We stood in ___ to remember the brave soldiers.
Soldiers ___ their comfort to keep us safe.

quiz.q: What does 'patriotism' mean?
quiz.explain: Patriotism is love and loyalty for one's country.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word

quiz.q: What does 'valour' mean?
quiz.explain: Valour means bravery, especially in battle.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'valour' with 'value'

quiz.q: What is India's highest wartime gallantry award?
quiz.explain: The Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award. Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award; the Arjuna Award is for sports.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up gallantry awards with civilian or sports awards

quiz.q: What is India's highest peacetime gallantry award?
quiz.explain: The Ashoka Chakra is the highest gallantry award for bravery away from the battlefield.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the wartime and peacetime awards

quiz.q: Where is the National War Memorial?
quiz.explain: The National War Memorial is in New Delhi, near India Gate.
quiz.mistake: Guesses another big city

quiz.q: What does 'sacrifice' mean?
options: giving up something precious for others
quiz.explain: Soldiers sacrifice comfort, time with family and sometimes their lives.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word

quiz.q: Which word is a synonym of 'brave'?
quiz.explain: Valiant means brave. The others mean fearful.
quiz.mistake: Picks an antonym instead of a synonym

quiz.q: Which word is the opposite of 'brave'?
quiz.explain: Cowardly means lacking courage — the opposite of brave.
quiz.mistake: Picks a synonym instead of an antonym

teach.ask: Gappu saw people standing silently at a war memorial. Why do they do that? Explain sacrifice and patriotism.
teach.praise: I'll bow my little head too. Thank you, brave soldiers.
teach.nudge: What did the soldiers give for the country, and how do we honour them?

learn.hook: 'The soldier saved the child' or 'The child was saved by the soldier' — same event, different focus!
points: In the active voice, the subject does the action: The soldiers built the bridge.
In the passive voice, the subject receives the action: The bridge was built by the soldiers.
Passive = a form of 'be' + past participle (+ by the doer).
Simple present passive: is/are + past participle. Simple past passive: was/were + past participle.
We use the passive when the doer is unknown or less important: The fort was built long ago.

example.q: Change to passive: 'The Navy rescued the fishermen.'
steps: Past tense, plural subject → were + past participle 'rescued'.
example.answer: The fishermen were rescued by the Navy.

learn.reallife: News reports often use the passive: 'Hundreds of people were rescued from the floods.'

games.title: Active or passive?
items: The soldiers built a bridge.
The captain hoisted the flag.
The pilot flew the plane.
The army helps the villagers.
A bridge was built by the soldiers.
The flag was hoisted by the captain.
The plane was flown by the pilot.
The villagers are helped by the army.

games.title: Build a passive sentence
items: The injured man
was carried
to the camp
by the soldiers.

quiz.q: Change to passive: 'The soldiers built the bridge.'
options: The soldiers were built by the bridge.
The bridge was built by the soldiers.
The bridge is building by the soldiers.
quiz.explain: The object becomes the subject; past tense → was + built; add 'by the soldiers'.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the words without changing the verb correctly

quiz.q: Change to passive: 'The army helps the villagers.'
options: The villagers is helped by the army.
The army is helped by the villagers.
The villagers are helped by the army.
The villagers were helped by the army.
quiz.explain: Simple present with a plural subject → are + helped.
quiz.mistake: Changes the tense while changing the voice

quiz.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The captain is hoisting the flag.
The flag was hoisted by the captain.
The captain will hoist the flag.
quiz.explain: The subject (the flag) receives the action, and the verb is was + hoisted.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any past tense sentence is passive

quiz.q: Change to active: 'The medal was given by the President.'
options: The President was given the medal.
quiz.explain: The doer (the President) becomes the subject; 'was given' becomes 'gave'.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the passive verb or changes the tense

quiz.q: 'The parade ___ watched by thousands of people.'
quiz.explain: 'Parade' is singular, so we use 'was' + watched.
quiz.mistake: Matches the verb to 'people' instead of the subject 'parade'

quiz.q: 'The letters were ___ by the soldiers.'
quiz.explain: The passive needs the past participle: write – wrote – written.
quiz.mistake: Uses the simple past instead of the past participle

quiz.q: 'The rescue boats ___ sent by the Navy.'
quiz.explain: 'Boats' is plural and the action is in the past, so 'were' is correct.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'was' with a plural subject

quiz.q: Why is the passive used in 'The fort was built long ago'?
options: The doer is unknown or not important
quiz.explain: We don't know or need to say who built the fort, so the passive fits.
quiz.mistake: Does not know when the passive is useful

teach.ask: Gappu read 'The village was saved by the soldiers' and asked who did the action. Explain active and passive voice.
teach.praise: So the soldiers did the saving! Passive puts the village first. Clever!
teach.nudge: Which voice puts the doer first, and which puts the receiver first?
